key_insight: A PPO-based controller can coordinate battery, hydrogen, diesel, and grid exchange in a community microgrid to maximize revenue while keeping load served very high under uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: The study shows how reinforcement learning can improve operational resilience and renewable utilization in hybrid microgrids with coupled storage and variable demand.
method: Modeled the microgrid as an MDP with 11 state variables and 3 continuous actions for battery, diesel, and hydrogen dispatch.
Used proximal policy optimization (PPO) for hourly energy management in a grid-connected PV-wind-battery-hydrogen system.
Evaluated performance over 8,760 hourly observations for a 1,000-household community in Rockhampton, Australia.
evidence_signal: Across a full-year simulation, the policy achieved A$195,690.67 net annual operating revenue, 91.2% renewable fraction, 99.77% load satisfaction, and retained 98.79% demand supply even when outage probability rose from 1% to 5%.
watch_item: Performance is sensitive to renewable-profile variability and training stability, and results depend on the chosen carbon-accounting boundary.
paper_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Energy Management for Hydrogen-Enabled Community Microgrids Under Uncertainty
